profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record in Tulsa County, Oklahoma, is tagged telecom=data_center under the name OCOSA, a short capitalized acronym with no obvious or widely recognized expansion. Acronym style names of this kind are common among small regional service companies, homeowners associations, government or quasi governmental bodies, and consortiums, so the acronym alone offers little basis for classifying what kind of organization, if any, OCOSA actually is. Public location records tie the coordinates behind this entry to the Deco District in downtown Tulsa, in the vicinity of a bank tower rather than a purpose built data center campus, which is consistent with the possibility that OCOSA designates equipment, a server room, or a tenant space inside a larger downtown office building rather than a freestanding facility. No operator website, press coverage, business registration, or permit record naming OCOSA as a data center operator could be located. Downtown bank and office towers commonly host telecom equipment rooms, colocation cages, or carrier hotel space that would reasonably be tagged as a data center point on a map without representing a standalone company, and that remains a plausible explanation here. Absent a confirmed operator, published capacity figures, or any other verifiable detail, this entry is presented honestly as an unresolved OpenStreetMap tag rather than a confirmed facility profile.

reading.body:
OCOSA is listed in OpenStreetMap as a data center in Tulsa County, Oklahoma, but the tag cannot be verified. Reverse geocoding of the coordinates points to a bank tower in downtown Tulsa's Deco District rather than a purpose-built data center campus. No operator website, business registration, press coverage, or permit record naming OCOSA as a data center operator could be found. The entry appears to mark either an equipment room or carrier hotel space inside an office building rather than a standalone facility.

No capacity figures are published for this site. Without specifications, it is not possible to assess its scale or relevance to AI infrastructure growth.

Oklahoma has nine mapped data center facilities on record and zero published megawatt figures across the state. This site cannot be ranked against peers because no operator has disclosed capacity. If OCOSA exists as a named standalone operator, its specifications remain unpublished.
